xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2564: feat(beads): Dolt-native cross-machine authority, synchronization, and dashboard freshness

plan.title: feat(beads): Dolt-native cross-machine authority, synchronization, and dashboard freshness
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: Beads made Dolt the only storage backend and demoted .beads/issues.jsonl to a derived export, but Overdeck is still mixed-authority and split-brained: runtime paths parse issues.jsonl directly, agents mutate beads with raw bd shell commands, the Dolt DB never travels between machines (only the JSONL rides overdeck-state), and this machine already has two divergent 1.1G Dolt DBs for the same project. The Machine A creates → Machine B closes → Machine C sees flow is not guaranteed. The PRD at drafts/pan-2564.md (revision 2, reconciled against the GPT-5 review) is the authoritative design.
narratives.Proposal: Dolt is canonical and travels on the project git remote at refs/dolt/data. One physical local Dolt home per project (state-worktree .beads, all checkouts redirect to it). One read door (resolver over bd --json) and one write door (runMutationBatch: lock once, pull once, mutate, commit once, export once, push once, typed conflict on rejection). Agents mutate only through pan beads verbs; a bd PATH shim mechanically rejects raw mutation verbs. A single-owner background synchronizer keeps the dashboard fresh with lastSyncedAt/stale surfaces. JSONL becomes a validated derived export. A cutover-marker state machine gates state migration; an isolated full-fidelity reconciliation report gates each project's operational cutover; this machine (panopticon-cli) cuts over inside this issue, including the designated-migrator bd >= 1.1.0 schema migration to v53.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No Dolt database bytes or runtime files ever committed to overdeck-state or any code branch
- No cross-machine single-writer coordinator service (divergence resolved via bd 1.1.0 native pull merge + typed conflicts)
- No unattended dolt.auto-push and no bd dolt push --force anywhere
- No JSONL-seeded live authority for remote Fly workspaces (remote work is mechanically blocked for migrated projects until authenticated Dolt-remote routing exists)
- Per-project operational cutovers for krux, lexerra, myn, myn-cli, tindra are operator-reviewed rollouts tracked outside this plan's beads (only panopticon-cli cutover is code-blocking)
- No changes to the beads/bd upstream binary itself (no fork, no patches)
- No beads UI redesign beyond the freshness/stale surfaces on the existing BeadsRail

autoDecisions.summary: Adopted PRD rev-2 (overdeck-state drafts/pan-2564.md) as the authoritative design without re-litigating decisions D1-D8/D-HOME/D-MARKER.
autoDecisions.rationale: The PRD was authored today, revised specifically to resolve all 15 findings of the GPT-5 review, and every file reference was re-verified in this workspace during planning.

autoDecisions.summary: Bead granularity: one bead per PRD work item, splitting WI-12 into cross-machine integration tests vs. this-machine cutover, and WI-13 into pan beads verbs vs. bd shim + prompt/skill enforcement.
autoDecisions.rationale: Each WI is already one focused, independently testable change with named tests; the two splits separate 'and'-joined deliverables with different risk profiles (test authoring vs. live data cutover; new CLI surface vs. enforcement sweep).

autoDecisions.summary: requiresInspection true only on beads-home (deep) and write-door (fast).
autoDecisions.rationale: These are the two foundations whose wrong implementation would force redoing most downstream beads (wrong physical DB resolved everywhere; wrong batch/push semantics baked into every mutation surface). All other beads fail loudly at typecheck/tests/review.

autoDecisions.summary: The work agent implements in this pipeline workspace on feature/pan-2564; the PRD section-7 mention of a bypass/pan-2564 branch is superseded.
autoDecisions.rationale: That line described a bypass-mode execution plan; this issue now runs through the normal pipeline, and worktree discipline forbids checking out another branch inside the workspace.

autoDecisions.summary: The bd >= 1.1.0 fleet upgrade and v32→v53 schema migration execute inside the cutover-panopticon bead as the designated migrator, after the home is unified; the version-policy bead only defines the minimum-version resolver.
autoDecisions.rationale: The 2026-07-12 1.1.0 trial proved upgrading before home unification breaks writes and risks schema forking; the PRD makes the safe ordering normative (unify home, migrate once, push, others bootstrap).

narrative.Action: Implement PRD WI-3 (decisions D6, C3). New src/lib/beads/writer.ts exposes runMutationBatch({ project, reason }, async (bd) => {...}): acquire the project lock once → ensureBootstrapped() → bd dolt pull once → run the callback operations → validate → commit once → export once (via jsonl-export module) → bd dolt push once → return { ok } | { conflict, localHead, remoteHead }. Single claim/close is a one-op batch. Failure atomicity: a failed op/validation reverts the Dolt working set, or if revert is unsafe returns typed needsOperatorRecovery — never commits or pushes a partial plan. On push rejection return the typed conflict with no --force; the next pull's bd 1.1.0 cascade-repair merge resolves. Route createBeadsFromVBrief, initializeWorkspaceBeads, the pan done close path, and label/status updates through the writer. pan done treats a close as durable ONLY after its batch push succeeds.

narrative.Action: Implement PRD WI-5. New src/dashboard/server/services/beads-sync-service.ts with ONE owner — the dashboard server process (not per-route, not per-tab) — running the background synchronizer with defined interval + jitter + backoff; it holds the project lock only for the bounded pull, off the request path, using execAsync/spawn (never execSync; delays via await new Promise). On a head-advancing pull it invalidates the issue's beads query server-side and emits a named domain event in the contracts schema over the existing /ws/rpc WebSocket; the frontend handler calls queryClient.invalidateQueries(['beads', issueId]). The 10-second UI poll triggers no network pull. BeadsRail renders lastSyncedAt, freshness age, and a stale/error badge. All interval/backoff tests use vi.useFakeTimers + advanceTimersByTimeAsync. narrative.Action: Implement PRD WI-7 (decision D7). New pan admin beads reconcile <project>: (1) take independent safety exports/snapshots FIRST; (2) clone refs/dolt/data into an ISOLATED temp DB (git fetch the ref into a scratch clone + bd bootstrap there) — never bd dolt pull into the live DB; (3) inventory the exact Dolt tables/columns used by beads 1.1.0 + Overdeck and enumerate them in the report; (4) compare normalized issue rows + labels + dependencies + comments + non-issue/config records + Dolt heads across {live local Dolt, isolated ref clone, overdeck-state issues.jsonl}; (5) distinguish 'absent' from 'outside export scope' (issue-only vs --all); (6) verify counts + sample-resolve; (7) emit a deterministic report (--json option) to ${OVERDECK_HOME}/state/<project>/notes/beads-reconcile-<date>.md plus a review/approval artifact that, once approved, feeds the cutover marker. The command NEVER imports, pushes, deletes, or selects a winner.

The designated-migrator migration preserves issue counts (pre/post bd list --all counts equal) and refs/dolt/data on origin advances to the migrated head
A valid beads-cutover.json persists for panopticon-cli and pan admin state migrate then passes the Dolt gate staging zero Dolt bytes
Documentation: BEADS.md, AGENT-STATE-PLANES.md, beads.mdx, CLAUDE.md sections, derived-JSONL rule

expected_outputs: lint (including lint-skills cross-check) passes; each named doc contains the required new sections

narrative.Action: Implement PRD WI-11. Update/create: docs/BEADS.md (embedded vs server mode, canonical-home/redirect model, designated-migrator + bd bootstrap schema-adoption procedure, Machine A→B→C lifecycle, recovery procedure, stale-state UI behavior); docs/AGENT-STATE-PLANES.md (beads plane = Dolt/refs/dolt/data, not overdeck-state); user-facing configuration/beads.mdx; the CLAUDE.md 'Beads Issue Tracker' and 'Session Completion' sections (agents use pan beads ..., not raw bd); and a bundled rule (sync-sources/rules/beads-derived-jsonl.md) stating issues.jsonl is derived-only and beads mutations go through pan beads. Wrapper-skill updates for changed CLI verbs land per the skills convention.

items.title: docs/AGENT-STATE-PLANES.md contains the statement that the beads plane travels on refs/dolt/data (not overdeck-state), and docs/BEADS.md covers the canonical-home/redirect model and the Machine A→B→C lifecycle with the bootstrap procedure
CLAUDE.md beads sections instruct pan beads mutations and no doc instructs raw mutating bd; grep for 'bd close'/'bd update' guidance in docs returns only the shim-rejection explanation
The new bundled rule ships in sync-sources/rules/ with scope frontmatter and renders into the harness context files after pan sync
